article.summary: The catalogued Dynamics-memory repository locator now redirects to 1173591564/memory-manage. At its verified default-branch head, the repository README identifies tasklog as the current runnable project and references Dynamics-memory as prior research. This review describes the current pinned tasklog code and documents the identity shift; it does not attribute uninspected historical Dynamics-memory internals to that code.

architecture.text: The catalogued URL redirects to the canonical repository 1173591564/memory-manage. GitHub repository metadata identifies mvp-2 as the default branch, whose README calls tasklog the current runnable project and lists Dynamics-memory in prior research notes. The current default-branch review therefore describes tasklog and does not claim the old Dynamics-memory implementation is still the active system.

Tasklog is a local-first event-history memory layer for coding agents. Its SQLite schema stores events as the fine-grained records, tasks as inferred or user-correctable groupings, task edges for parent/continue/supersede relationships, extracted symbols, full-text indexes, and optional raw-source identity fields. The types explicitly define no Memory or Summary object.

The default database is .tasklog/log.db under a configured project root; large event outputs are stored separately as hash-addressed blobs. The schema records session/sequence/time, role, event kind, tool call/result linkage, outcome, task assignment, and source/source_id/source_ref.
The MCP server exposes tasklog queries and describes when to consult history versus current code; the system is designed for project coding history rather than general cross-project knowledge memory.

behavior.text: Write: the event ingestion path inserts captured events, extracts code symbols mechanically, updates the full-text index, and writes oversized outputs to blob files while retaining a locator and short mechanical preview. The README characterizes the write path as zero LLM calls.

Update and task organization: imported source records use source plus source_id as an idempotence key; task segmentation and supersedes relationships organize events without replacing the event log. The reviewed MCP tools are read-oriented and do not expose a memory edit or delete operation. No end-to-end ingestion or mutation sequence was run.

Delete: no deletion or erasure API was found in the reviewed query/MCP surface. This bounded source inspection does not establish what maintenance or direct database operations may exist elsewhere in the repository, nor does it establish physical erasure of blobs or backups.

Retrieval: list_tasks provides a task directory; search_history searches event history and may filter by task/symbol; symbol_history performs indexed lookup; resume_task returns a task-oriented state reconstruction; read_events pages original records; read_blob retrieves large outputs. Results carry event/task/session/sequence locators for follow-up reads.

Scope isolation: the default SQLite database is stored under the project root, with TASKLOG_REPO and TASKLOG_DB allowing callers to configure the root and database path. This gives a filesystem-level per-project layout, but the reviewed stdio MCP server has no caller authentication or tenant authorization layer; isolation depends on deployment and filesystem boundaries.

Provenance and evidence: imported events can retain host name, stable source ID and raw source metadata separately from inferred sequence, role mapping or outcome. Event and blob locators allow evidence to be reopened. Task boundaries record their source/evidence and can be revised; source metadata does not itself validate the truth of event content.

Efficiency and observability: exact symbol indexes, SQLite FTS5/trigram search, indexed task/event fields, paging, bounded event previews, blob retrieval and optional vector search reduce the need to load whole histories. The CLI/MCP surface includes index health telemetry; the repository describes local metrics and adapters, but no runtime latency, token, cost or storage result was collected.

limits.text: The repository locator now resolves to memory-manage, where the default branch describes tasklog as the current project and treats Dynamics-memory as prior research. The review records that transition and assesses current tasklog code; continuity between the catalog label and the current project beyond the redirect and repository documentation is not independently established.

This bounded inspection covered the root and tasklog READMEs, database schema/opening, core types, ingestion, symbol extraction, queries, optional vector search, and MCP surface. It did not audit every adapter, task-boundary implementation, evaluation path, deployment, or external host integration.

Source inspection cannot establish retrieval effectiveness, abstention quality, correction/staleness rates, deletion leakage, deployment isolation, observed latency, token/cost consumption, or storage efficiency. No system runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.
